sentences.text: Trinacromerum was an extinct sauropterygian reptile, a group of marine animals, that reached a body length of nearly 3 meters.
Richard Ellis described its physical appearance as resembling a "four-flippered penguin," while the name Trinacromerum translates to "three tipped femur."
Its long flippers allowed it to swim at high speeds, a unique adaptation for its time.
The genus Trinacromerum was first described by Cragin in 1888.
The genus includes species such as T. bentonianum, T. latimanus, T. kirki, and T. bonneri.
Evidence from its teeth indicates that Trinacromerum fed on small fish.
The long flippers of Trinacromerum allowed it to reach high swimming speeds.
Trinacromerum is classified within the family Polycotylidae and the subfamily Polycotylinae.
The type species of the genus Trinacromerum is Trinacromerum bentonianum.
Trinacromerum lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically from the Albian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 106.3 and 66 million years ago.
Fossils of Trinacromerum have been found in Late Cretaceous deposits in modern-day Kansas and Manitoba.
